Retrieval note: the live mass.gov domain returned HTTP 403 'This page is forbidden' to every non-interactive fetch attempted in this session (plain curl with full browser headers, and this session's WebFetch tool) -- a bot-detection/WAF block, not a sign the document is gone. A live Chrome browser session (via this session's browser-automation tool) did successfully load mass.gov RMV pages, confirming the block is bot-fingerprint-based rather than a dead link, but that tool's script-injection-based content-extraction functions (page-text/read/screenshot) were malfunctioning session-wide at the time (they failed even on http://example.com), so on-page text could not be captured that way either. Given that, the manual was retrieved from the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine, which had crawled and cached the exact same official mass.gov PDF at the exact same canonical URL above. Verified via the Wayback CDX API (which also shows mass.gov began 403-blocking the Wayback crawler itself starting in 2024, so no newer capture exists to retrieve), the most recent successful archived capture of the actual PDF is timestamped 2023-05-11 17:02:48 UTC, snapshot digest 75RJ2QY3SXNVCNUNEXC3PXUIM447LJ44, fetched via https://web.archive.org/web/20230511170248id_/https://www.mass.gov/doc/drivers-manual/download -- a genuine PDF (not an HTML/error page), downloaded losslessly and converted to text with pdftotext -layout (native text extraction, not OCR). The PDF's own cover states it is the 'Revised December 2022' edition -- the newest edition this session could independently verify; a newer edition may exist that could not be checked given the live-site block, and no assumption is made about undocumented later changes. Full text (with a provenance header) archived to temp/handbooks/ma/driver.txt. Exam mechanics were NOT guessed -- they are stated verbatim in the manual itself (Chapter 1, 'Learner's Permit Exam Procedures,' p.22): 'Each learner's permit exam has 25 multiple-choice questions ... To pass the exam, you must answer 18 questions correctly within the allotted time of 25 minutes.' That gives 25 items, a 72% (18/25) passing score, and a 25-minute time limit; topics covered per the manual are 'alcohol misuse, suspensions, and JOL violations, as well as rules of the road and identifying road signs.' Content depth: this is an unusually rich, detailed manual (about 8,680 lines / 466KB of extracted text spanning 6 chapters plus appendices) with substantial, well-differentiated sections on licensing and the Junior Operator (GDL) law, violations/points/suspensions, OUI/alcohol/drug law, seatbelt and child-passenger law, the hands-free/distracted-driving law, defensive driving and stopping distances, speed limits, traffic signals (including MA-specific devices like Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons and Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons), signs, railroad crossings, work zones, pavement markings (including an unusually detailed bicycle-infrastructure section: sharrows, bike boxes, green pavement, separated lanes), lanes/intersections/turns, right-of-way including Massachusetts-specific rotaries and roundabouts, passing, an extensive 'sharing the road' set (school buses, trucks, trolleys, funeral processions, animals, motorcycles) with a notably detailed bicyclist-law section (Chap. 85 Sec. 11B), parking, emergency-vehicle/move-over law and police-stop guidance, driving emergencies (skids, blowouts, brake failure, railroad-track stalls, tunnels), crash reporting, and vehicle equipment/registration/inspection/insurance basics. This comfortably supported 315 distinct, grounded, non-repetitive multiple-choice questions across 24 topic buckets before deduplication, all traceable to specific manual sections cited in each question's source_note -- no invented facts, no generic 'common driving knowledge' not actually present in this manual.
